editorial:
Imagine being a super strict priest who lives by the rules, only to wake up one day with no idea who you are. That is exactly what happens to Serge. He is a frail guy who takes his faith very seriously until a bad fall wipes his memory. Suddenly, he is rescued by Albine, a free spirit who doesn't care about the church. Her uncle is an atheist who loves to argue, which makes the house a very funny and tense place to be. You get to see Serge transform from a stiff man of God into a happy, relaxed guy who is deeply in love with a woman he is supposed to avoid. It is a sweet but stressful setup that feels like a slow burn drama.

The acting is great because you can really feel the guilt building up as Serge starts to remember his old life. The pace is a bit slow, but it helps you feel the weight of his choice. If you like stories about forbidden love and internal struggle, you will really enjoy this. Since it is an older film, you should look for the best version possible. Try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection to see the beautiful scenery in high quality. It is a great pick for a quiet movie night.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when Serge finally gets his memory back. He remembers he is a priest and feels like he has committed a huge sin by loving Albine. He tries to go back to his strict religious life, but he cannot forget the happiness he felt with her. In the end, the guilt and the pressure are too much for him. He cannot balance his love for Albine with his duty to God, leading to a sad and broken spirit.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about faith, love, and difficult choices.
